source: Written by Claude (claude-opus-5-5) from the county counts (AP via The New York Times), the 2024 baseline and Census ACS 2023 context.

10001.t:
Kent County voted for Coons over Katz in the U.S. Senate race by 15 points, 36,401 votes to 27,009, with 99% of the expected vote counted. That is a 13-point move toward the Democrats from Harris's 2-point edge here in 2024, close to the state's 12-point shift and matching the typical Delaware county. Nationally, the typical county moved 14 points left.

Turnout was 63,410 votes, 72% of the 88,141 cast in 2024, so the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home. Among Delaware's three counties, all of which moved left, Kent's shift was smaller than Sussex's 14 points and larger than New Castle's 12. Kent cast the fewest votes of the three.

10005.t:
Sussex County backed Trump by 11 points in 2024 and flipped in the U.S. Senate race, giving Democrat Coons 59,196 votes to Republican Katz's 55,867, a margin of 3 points. That is a 14-point move toward the Democrats, the largest of Delaware's three counties, all of which moved left. The state as a whole moved 12 points, Kent 13 and New Castle 12, and Sussex was the only county to switch from a Trump win to a Democratic win. Nationally, the typical county moved 14 points.

There were 115,063 votes cast, 78% of the 2024 total. With that many fewer voters, the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home.

10003.t:
New Castle County, Delaware's largest by votes cast, gave Democrat Chris Coons a 45-point margin over Republican Mike Katz in the U.S. Senate race, 144,750 votes to 54,888. That is 12 points more Democratic than Harris's 33-point margin here in 2024, matching the statewide shift in a race the Democrat won by 27. Still, New Castle moved the least of Delaware's three counties: Kent shifted 13 points and Sussex 14, flipping from a Trump win to a narrow Democratic one. Nationally, the typical county moved 14 points left.

Turnout was 199,638 votes, 72% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell how much of the shift came from voters changing their minds and how much from who stayed home.
